disagreements.underlying_difference: The two positions optimise against different failure modes — conflicting implicit decisions versus context exhaustion — and both are coherent. The first is a practitioner position with a testable mechanism and no published measurement; the second is a measurement from a publisher that sells retrieval. R8 also notes the founder's requirement cannot then mean one store read by everyone; it must mean one AUTHORITY per field with delivery narrowed per attempt, and the thesis does not distinguish those designs.
disagreements.discriminator: The quantity neither side has measured: how much load-bearing content survives narrowing, against how much accuracy is lost by carrying it all. The package's own summary-loss instrument could measure the first.
disagreements.status: preserved; three lanes independently refused to resolve it

disagreements.topic: Is there a turning point in executor count?

position_a.claim: Performance under vote and filter-vote aggregation first increases then decreases with the number of calls, because more calls help easy queries and hurt hard ones in the same dataset.

position_b.claim: Sampling and voting scales with the number of agents instantiated.

disagreements.underlying_difference: Two primary sources, compatible only if the turning point sits beyond the second's sweep. Neither located it for agentic work. R8 adds vendor statements of diminishing returns and a 3–5 recommendation, which is direction and not a location.
disagreements.discriminator: The sweep the claim specifies (1, 3, 7, 15, 30 at fixed total capacity) — which R8 finds is forbidden by the package's concurrency policy, so the discriminator is blocked upstream. See axis X14.

disagreements.topic: Is the reported multi-agent gain architecture or resource?

position_a.claim: A 90.2% improvement over a single agent on an internal research evaluation, at roughly 15x the tokens of chat.

position_b.claim: At matched budget the advantage disappears; the same vendor's own variance decomposition attributes 80% of variance to token usage.

disagreements.underlying_difference: Budget matching, plus task shape. The vendor source itself excludes most coding work and names the unsuitable class. R8's reconciliation — research-like work parallelises, construction-like work does not — is an inference it declines to call settled.
disagreements.discriminator: Matched-capacity comparison run separately on a research-shaped task and a construction-shaped task, each reported beside its realised concurrency count.

disagreements.topic: Does the simple baseline minimise scarce subscription capacity?

position_a.claim: B0 is granted 'the lowest plausible consumption of scarce subscription capacity' among its legitimate strengths.

position_b.claim: Four documented mechanisms make one long session consume more allowance than its activity suggests — the full conversation is resent with every request, a break longer than the cache lifetime reprocesses the whole context, compaction is itself a large request, and idle check-ins send full context. Separately, a native job caps at a 360-second window, so a six-hour single context cannot run at all.

disagreements.underlying_difference: B0 minimises LAUNCHES. It does not minimise the WEEKLY BUCKET, and the weekly bucket is what binds. R2 removes a different strength on a different ground drawn from the package's own launch contract rather than from a vendor page.
disagreements.discriminator: Instrument the four mechanisms and measure B0's weekly-bucket draw against a continuation-based arm at matched accepted outcomes. Note the standing limit: there is no published absolute denominator, so the result can only be a ratio.
disagreements.status: preserved; neither lane amended the frozen protocol and both said so

position_a.claim: Vendor: three-level progressive disclosure means many skills can be installed without context penalty; the regime designed for is around 100 skills.

position_b.claim: Academic: hiding the skill body costs 37–44 points of routing accuracy on a roughly 80,000-skill overlapping registry, and body-distilled descriptions remain 7–21 points short.

disagreements.underlying_difference: Different quantities at library sizes roughly 600x apart — context tokens versus routing accuracy. R6 states they locate a crossover rather than contradict each other, and that the crossover is unknown.
disagreements.discriminator: Selection accuracy over a REAL skill corpus at 10, 100 and 1000 with adversarial near-duplicates, on a current model. Nobody has published it, and negative control §4.10 constrains who may author the near-duplicates.
disagreements.status: preserved; R6 explicitly declines to resolve

disagreements.topic: Do seeded defects estimate real-defect detection?

position_a.claim: Mutant detection correlates with real fault detection independently of coverage, and hand-seeded faults are not a good substitute while mutants are. (R7 could not open the primary; quotation is via a citing paper and a search summary.)

position_b.claim: All correlations between mutation scores and real fault detection are weak once test-suite size is controlled; mutants guide improvement, they do not estimate detection.

disagreements.underlying_difference: The two measure different dependent variables, which the later paper's own introduction notes. The later study is larger and controls the confound; R7 declines to conclude from that alone.
disagreements.discriminator: None needed for the operative use: under BOTH readings the control detects an always-pass checker and does not license a published detection rate.
disagreements.status: preserved per DIRECTIVE §6; practical consequence identical either way

disagreements.topic: Grade the outcome or the path?

position_a.claim: Vendor guidance: step-checking is too rigid and brittle, so grade what the agent produced, not the path it took.

position_b.claim: Wrong for this system: a benchmark comparing final state acknowledges that a passing episode can omit a required user confirmation. In a system whose fixed boundaries include who may release an external effect, a grader that scores only the product cannot see a skipped authorisation.

disagreements.underlying_difference: The vendor guidance is calibrated to coding agents where the product is the whole obligation. Here the path contains the obligation.
disagreements.discriminator: Plant a skipped-authorisation defect in an artifact whose final state is correct, and see whether the grader is capable of failing it.
disagreements.status: R7 contradicts the vendor deliberately and says which is conflicted

disagreements.topic: Is delegation depth a policy, a resource limit or a safety property?

position_a.claim: One vendor permits three layers below the main conversation and withholds the delegation tool at the limit, so work completes rather than failing. Depth is a configuration value.

position_b.claim: Another vendor forbids subagent recursion absolutely, even with wildcard tool access. Depth is an invariant.

disagreements.underlying_difference: Two vendors, one decision, opposite answers, both deliberate, same year. The evidence establishes only that delegation depth is a design choice with a named owner — which is exactly what the protocol requires of a candidate.
disagreements.discriminator: R3's own question: the answer decides who may change the ceiling and whether changing it is a self-modification requiring review. R4 sharpens it — in this runtime spawning costs no permission check at all, so the ceiling needs an owner AND a checkpoint.

disagreements.topic: What should happen to work nothing can currently handle?

position_a.claim: Park indefinitely and wait for a human to deploy a handler; state is not lost and the task retries after redeploy.

position_b.claim: Refuse with a recorded reason, as a terminal state of the same record.

position_c.claim: Assign by default to the next supervisory position and escalate on a timer.

disagreements.underlying_difference: Each has a different failure: an obligation with a deadline rots in the first, a real duty is declined in the second, and the third ends assigned and silent after a bounded number of repeats.
disagreements.discriminator: Run F-1's spurious job and a genuine-deadline variant under each disposition and count rotted obligations against wrongly declined duties. R5's own reading is that the right choice is almost certainly per consequence class rather than global.

position_a.claim: In ticket routing, any assignment to someone who cannot resolve the ticket is inefficient.

position_b.claim: Reassignments are useful for determining the best person to fix a bug, contrary to the popular opinion that they are always harmful; the harmful shape is cycles at the end of a sequence.

disagreements.underlying_difference: One treats re-routing as waste, the other as the diagnostic path by which the right owner is found.
disagreements.discriminator: Measure end-of-sequence cycles separately from reassignment count. A design that minimises re-routing may be suppressing diagnosis.

disagreements.topic: Buy a second model family, or stop relying on model judgement for the affected decisions?

position_a.claim: A panel of smaller judges from DISJOINT families beats a single large judge, with less intra-model bias, at over seven times lower cost; and the only working remedy for self-consistent errors was a cross-model probe.

position_b.claim: Error correlation persists across distinct architectures and providers and RISES with capability, so the strongest second opinion is the most correlated one; and on objectively checkable correctness, strong judges perform slightly better than random regardless of family.

disagreements.underlying_difference: Whether the residual after buying diversity is small enough to matter. The first position's cited mechanism is family disjointness, which a same-family panel has removed by construction.
disagreements.discriminator: Joint false acceptance measured on a controlled planted-defect set, same-family pair against cross-family pair. R7 searched and found no published comparison of exactly this.
disagreements.status: preserved; R7 states it is a decision and declines to make it

disagreements.topic: Are the founder's five axes separable in practice?

position_a.claim: Separable yes — each axis can vary alone; only exhaustiveness fails.

position_b.claim: In the shipping runtime a knowledge artifact carries a tool grant and can fork an isolated context, so the skills axis and the authority and context axes are not independently variable.

disagreements.underlying_difference: Separability in the TAXONOMY versus separability in the IMPLEMENTATION. R2's verdict is about the first and R2's own F-08 is about the second.
disagreements.discriminator: In the runtime that will actually be used, construct a skill carrying no tool grant and a tool grant carrying no procedure, and check whether either can be varied without touching the other.
disagreements.status: preserved; the tension is internal to R2 as well as across lanes

disagreements.topic: Is the coordination question a trichotomy or a quadrichotomy?

position_a.claim: Three loci, named at the source in 1986: in the knowledge sources, on the blackboard, in a separate module, or a combination.

position_b.claim: A fourth working arrangement exists and is neither: coordination by SUBSCRIPTION — structured messages published to a shared pool, extracted by role-specific interests, with activation gated on receiving all prerequisite dependencies.

disagreements.underlying_difference: Subscription is a control locus distributed across the readers rather than held by a module or by the record, and it is the one reading with a shipped implementation and reported scores.
disagreements.discriminator: Build the fixture under each reading and measure contradictory actions, duplicated external effects and owner minutes, per the claim's own measure — now with four arms rather than three.
disagreements.status: new; surfaced by putting two lanes side by side

disagreements.topic: A number in this repository's own decision record cannot be traced to its cited primary

position_a.claim: The decision record and two sections of an internal design document state evaluator agreement of 5–17% and per-evaluator detection of 18–60%, attributed to a 2003 review.

position_b.claim: The primary states 5–65% any-two agreement and per-evaluator detection of 59% and 45%; a third section of the same internal document states the traceable 5–65% version with 'verified' beside it. R7 searched the primary for both disputed ranges and found neither.

disagreements.underlying_difference: R7 does not assert the figures are wrong — they may derive from an internal sweep it did not locate — only that they cannot be traced from the repository's own citation, which makes them folklore under the evidence rules. The direction is primary-verified and unaffected: low pairwise agreement, largely distinct finding subsets, union far exceeding any single evaluator.
disagreements.discriminator: Locate the internal sweep that produced them, or re-derive from the primary and correct the record. Note that the unverifiable version is what propagated into the brief R7 itself was given.
disagreements.status: open, and it is a measurement-integrity finding against this round's own inputs

axes.movement: moved — an instrument now exists where there was none
axes.account: The first round distinguished purpose, instructions and continuing promises and left implementation open. F2 supplies a measurement: constraints and obligations survive transfer at roughly 0.57 while operational facts survive at roughly 0.97, and typed machine-actionable constraints reduced leakage to 0 of 48 where vague language leaked in 73% of cases [R2 F-04, R2 F-05]. Two further constituents were named as missing from any obligation record: surviving obligations that outlive their case and explicit contradiction state [R1 TC-14], and a reason-finished field separate from the status field, which shipped software makes optional [R5-13].
axes.discriminating_question: For each of the 46 capabilities, which carry constraints that would not survive a 25-word compression, and do those constraints travel as types or as prose?
axes.status: agreement on need; implementation open; now with a measurable survival rate

axes.movement: barely moved, and the evidence base itself was found to be narrow
axes.account: Make-versus-buy remains open. Two additions. A criterion that applies only to human performers was identified — professional standing that the act itself requires, which no capability difference can supply [R2 TC-38] — and a second, that a human is a differently-correlated error source [R7 §8 F-6]. Separately, every system in the framework survey is a software-construction or generic-orchestration system whose benchmarks measure repository issues, desktop tasks and multi-hop reasoning, so no evidence bears on customs disputes, refunds, supplier commitments or wind-down [R3 §9]. The narrowing risk named in W11 is a risk of importing the EVIDENCE BASE, not only the vocabulary.
axes.discriminating_question: Which responsibilities must be owned internally, and which of them does the round have any relevant evidence about at all?
axes.status: unresolved trade-off; evidence-base narrowness newly recorded

axes.round: F2 update — this round owns this axis
axes.account: Three changes. First, the arrangement the thesis describes is a named 1970s–80s architecture whose own author states no control component is specified and that the locus may sit in the knowledge sources, on the record, in a separate module, or in a combination — so the open question in the thesis is the hole the original model left, unclosed for forty years [R5-01]. Second, the cost of the explicit-coordinator reading is documented at the source: a monitor gains broad executive power that can violate the opportunism the shared record existed to enable [R5-02]. Third, a counter-mechanism was measured that none of the readings predicts: correlated reasoning produced 18 of 30 agents choosing one branch name with no shared state at all, and hidden-profile suppression means a shared consensus makes the related failure worse [R1 F-17]. A fourth locus was surfaced by comparison — coordination by subscription [R3 F33].
axes.discriminating_question: Under each of the four loci, how many contradictory actions, duplicated external effects and owner minutes occur — and does a shared authoritative view raise or lower duplicated external effects?
axes.status: foundational alternatives retained, now four rather than three, with one cost priced and one counter-mechanism measured

axes.movement: moved — two relied-upon defences are now measured and both fail against the attack that matters
axes.account: Write-path content screening refused 0 of 360 poisoned memories carrying no instruction, while detecting indirect prompt injection at 0.832 recall; read-path provenance ranking at its shipped weight was statistically indistinguishable from no defence and at its effective weight took evidence recall to exactly 0.00% [R1 F-10]. A retrieved wrong fact overrides correct prior knowledge over 60% of the time [R1 F-11]. One reading of a single source of truth has a production existence proof for exactly one fact class, at the price of a dedicated global service and a bespoke consistency mechanism [R1 F-23]. Two structural mechanisms arrived from the framework survey: a state write as an appended event, so state and audit trail are one artifact, and single-writer concurrency keyed per entity [R3 F24, R3 F25, R3 F42].
axes.discriminating_question: How is a plausible wrong fact — one carrying no attack signature — detected, and what is the blast radius and time-to-detection when it is not?
axes.status: empirical and semantic disagreement retained; the package's two named defences are now evidenced against

axes.movement: moved — the distinctions now carry magnitudes, and one internal figure was corrected
axes.account: Exact-match judge agreement overstates chance-corrected agreement by 33.8–41.2 points on the benchmark most often cited, putting the familiar 80% figure at a moderate kappa [R7 F3]. Test-retest reliability above 0.95 coexists with substantial position bias — reproducible and invalid at once [R7 F4]. On objectively checkable correctness, strong judges perform slightly better than random [R7 F5]. Withholding producer framing moves the DECISION THRESHOLD and not the DISCRIMINATION, because the same judges flag 68.4–96.8% of already-patched files under neutral framing [R7 F8]. The best procedurally independent reviewer measured reaches 28.6% F1 [R7 F9]. Human evaluators agree with each other 5–65% and on severity 20–28% [R7 F15]. One repository figure was found untraceable from its own citation [R7 F16].
axes.discriminating_question: What is the joint false-acceptance rate of a same-family producer/checker pair on a controlled planted-defect set, with a paired clean case run in the same session?
axes.status: agreement on distinctions; completeness unproven; magnitudes now attached and unflattering

axes.movement: moved — the invariant is unchanged and the enforcement options are now named, with one buildable path and one measured delivery failure
axes.account: Attenuation is solved and shipped in three production families, all putting it in the credential or the call rather than in the holder [R4 F2]; it buys narrowing and not revocation, and revocation requires a live re-read at the enforcement point at the moment of the effect [R4 F3]. The default runtime inherits authority in four documented ways [R4 F5]. A deterministic per-agent attenuation path exists today, outside the model, via a pre-tool hook carrying the caller's identity plus a deny-first non-overridable precedence [R4 F7]. Four vulnerability records show confused deputy at production scale, all scope-changed [R4 F9]. No standardised mechanism verifies that a delegation chain narrows [R4 F10]. From the framework side: an approval interrupt can re-run its node from the top and duplicate the effect it was approving [R3 F29, R3 F30], and a grant was observed to narrow reliably and arrive unreliably [R3 F59].
axes.discriminating_question: Does this system have a credential at the boundary at all — and if not, must the constraint be enforced by mediation rather than by delegation, which is a different architecture?
axes.status: agreement on the invariant; enforcement options open; the default configuration currently violates it

axes.round: F2 update — this round owns this axis
axes.movement: left where it was, with two new constraints and no validation
axes.account: No founder-specific dose is validated and none became validated. The specified transfer test is unexecuted in the literature [R1 TC-29]; nothing in the entire framework survey measures whether a system's human operator can still judge the work [R3 §9]; and the human anchor is itself an instrument with a measured error rate, which nothing in the package states or requires to be measured [R7 F15, R7 §9]. Two constraints are new: the founder's value as a checker is that his errors are uncorrelated with the model family's, so a week of his absence removes the system's only cross-family error source [R7 §8 F-6]; and the structure that is easiest for a founder to hold is the one W11 rejects by name, which is a criterion tension rather than a defect [R8 A-6].
axes.discriminating_question: What dose of returned work preserves competence, what is the founder's own expected error rate, and what does the system decline to accept during his absence for that reason?

axes.movement: moved substantially, and the central reading inverted
axes.account: Under subscription capacity, architecture does not change what the company spends; it changes the date on which work stops [R8 §3]. Unused allowance is destroyed rather than banked, so a conservative reservation is waste rather than thrift [R8 §3]. There is no published absolute denominator on the provider side, so every capacity finding this round can produce is a ratio between arms [R8 W-6]. A parallel executor's prompt cache expires far sooner than the main session's, so splitting costs more allowance than token arithmetic predicts [R8 W-2]; at the current concurrency pin, thirty executors cost thirty serialised launches rather than thirty concurrent windows [R8 W-1]. The no-silent-metered-fallback rule has no mechanism and the fallback is one setting away at both providers [R8 W-5]. From the specification side, a native job caps at a 360-second window, so continuation is mandatory in every arm [R2 F-18].
axes.discriminating_question: If a provider doubled or halved the allowance overnight, would any decision in this round change? If none would, the capacity argument was never load-bearing.
axes.status: unresolved feasibility trade-off, now stated in the right units with the denominator missing

axes.movement: barely moved; two new instances of the same tension
axes.account: A peer work projection is a derivative of another venture's work that may outlive the grant that justified it, and erasure does not propagate to derivatives by default [R1 §9.5, R1 §9.7]. High-risk-system event logging is a legal obligation whose scope for these ventures nobody in the round owns, which closes any future argument that the manifest can be dropped on cost grounds without checking scope first [R1 F-22]. A skill retired out from under an accepted run breaks that run's pinned references, and no retirement rule names a citation check [R6 §9 Q5].
axes.discriminating_question: When a grant is revoked or a record erased, what happens to every derivative already written — projections, summaries, pinned skill versions and accepted runs that cite them?

axes.round: F2 update — this round owns this axis
axes.movement: moved — a removal test now has a named exemplar
axes.account: The research group that established that agent-computer interface design measurably changes behaviour now ships a hundred-line successor that deletes the interface engineering, keeps one tool and a linear history, and scores competitively — so a scaffold's contribution is a function of the model generation that motivated it and must be re-ablated when the model changes [R3 F38, R3 F39]. Which harness mechanisms carry a removal test remains unanswered, and a mechanism with no removal criterion is a permanent tax that W9 makes a failure condition [R3 §10.6]. On libraries, corpus quality rather than retrieval is the limiting factor, and compact curated content beat comprehensive documentation by nearly four times [R6 F5, R6 F4]. Determinism is the only lever that reduces subscription consumption without reducing work, and it belongs to every position [R8 B-7].
axes.discriminating_question: For each mechanism a candidate proposes, what evidence would cause its removal, and who re-runs that test when the model generation changes?
axes.status: agreement on tests; change allocation open; one exemplar of a scaffold correctly removed

axes.topic: The unit of justification for an executor
axes.account: The five criteria do not share a unit. Parallel work predicates on a running instance and only relative to a chosen partition; distinct tools or permissions on a permission scope that may outlive any instance; isolated context on a context boundary; specialized knowledge on a template or skill version; independent verification on a relation between two instances, a property of neither alone [R2 F-20]. The measured verification effect attaches to a separate CONTEXT and a separate INPUT SET, which are cheaper than an agent [R7 §9]. Version, owner, provenance and deprecation are properties of the DISTRIBUTION unit in every system examined [R6 F9]. And for authority the unit is whatever is checked at the moment of the effect [R4 F1]. A criterion applied to the wrong unit returns undecidable, and undecidable reads as satisfied.
axes.discriminating_question: Applied to each candidate unit — template, instance, standing role, context boundary, permission scope, distribution unit, input set — which of the five criteria returns a decidable answer, and which returns undecidable?

axes.account: A major vendor implements both and states they are not interchangeable: a handoff is used when routing is part of the work and the specialist should own the remainder of the turn; agents-as-tools when a specialist should help with a bounded subtask without taking over [R2 F-17]. Combined with measured constraint loss, a handoff is the construct that discards boundary metadata because it transfers OWNERSHIP OF THE TURN through a compressed artifact, while consultation keeps the obligation-holder in place [R2 F-17, R2 F-04]. A second vendor's default handoff does the opposite — it transfers the entire prior conversation and leaves the guardrails behind, scoped to the first and last agent only [R3 F20, R3 F21]. And the system hands off to ITSELF on every job longer than the launch window [R2 F-18].
axes.discriminating_question: For each transfer a candidate defines: does the obligation-holder leave the turn, what typed constraints travel, and is a continuation across a launch boundary held to the same discipline as an inter-agent handoff?

axes.account: They are separate classes with different survival rates under the same transformation — roughly 0.97 against roughly 0.57 — so any single aggregate loss figure describes neither [R2 F-04, R2 F-05]. Compaction's documented loss shape is early material, middle material and material the summariser cannot see is load-bearing, which is the shape of an exclusion, a rejected alternative and a promised remedy [R1 F-01, R1 INFERENCE from F-01 to F-05]. The same class appears in procedural knowledge as the stale skill whose example omits a duty, and nothing in any skill format checks a duty [R6 FC-5].
axes.discriminating_question: Measured separately, what fraction of constraints survives each transformation in the system — and which of the 46 capabilities carry constraints that would not survive the compression the system actually performs?

axes.topic: The concurrency pin as containment versus as a demand on the round
axes.account: The current concurrency policy is one native job plus one external job, and the external profile is not yet admitted [R2 F-19]. That makes TC-03, TC-20 and TC-39 unmeasurable as specified, and the parallelism half of TC-22 with them [R8 §5, R2 TC-03]. Raising it requires a reviewed plan revision after measured evidence, so the measurement that would set the threshold requires first changing the parameter being measured [R8 TC-39]. And no inspected page establishes any account-level concurrency entitlement, so the pin may be a self-imposed policy rather than a provider constraint [R8 §6 unknowns, R8 §10 Q7].
axes.discriminating_question: Is the pin a provider constraint or a policy? If policy, who owns a bounded capacity trial with a stopping rule; if a provider constraint, which thesis claims are permanently unmeasurable in this system and does the round say so in those words?

axes.topic: The simple baseline's granted strengths are not purchasable as written
axes.account: The protocol grants B0 the lowest plausible consumption of scarce subscription capacity; four documented provider mechanisms contradict that clause [R8 B-6]. The protocol's B0 is 'one long-context session'; the package's own launch contract caps a native job at a 360-second window, so a long single context cannot run and continuation is mandatory in every arm [R2 F-18]. B0 has no verification independence of any kind by construction, and the checker it would be compared against measures 28.6% F1, so B0 plus deterministic scripts plus human acceptance is not obviously worse than B0 plus a same-family checker [R7 §8]. Neither lane amended the frozen protocol, and both said so explicitly.
axes.discriminating_question: At what added mechanism has the simple baseline rebuilt the case-admission authority and stopped being the simple baseline — and what is its real weekly-bucket draw once the four provider mechanisms are instrumented?

axes.account: One grant delivered 24 tools on one date and zero across three independent dispatches two days later with configuration unchanged, cause unknown; attenuation held, delivery did not [R3 F59]. One harness deleted 44 capability declarations no configuration backed and 16 budget blocks nothing read, and three of four workflow files are invoked by nothing [R3 F60]. A lint rule in the same harness records its own limit in its source: it checks the DECLARATION, not the BINDING [R3 F57]. And a capability declared in a file and never re-checked at the effect is a job title with a different noun [R4 F1]. This round supplies its own instance: seven of eight lanes reported the claim-registration tool absent from their sessions while the roster declares the grant.
axes.discriminating_question: Can a grant be observed to have ARRIVED, as distinct from having been declared — and what does a task that silently did less look like from the outside?

axes.account: Every privacy and filtering source located measures leakage and none measures correct work refused because the loader filtered too hard; the extreme case is a defence that took evidence recall to exactly 0.00% while becoming statistically effective [R1 §9.1, R1 F-10]. The same asymmetry appears in verification: the neutrally framed judges that 'detect' at 97.2% also flag 96.8% of already-fixed files, so detection without a paired clean case is a constant rather than a measurement [R7 F8, R7 M4]. A shipping evaluation tool encodes the discipline by excluding graders that cannot fail in the baseline arm [R6 F8].
axes.discriminating_question: For every filtering, trust and refusal mechanism the system proposes, what is the rate of correct work refused, measured in the same session as the adverse case?

axes.topic: The interval between declared done and accepted
axes.account: Every surveyed system terminates at producer-declared completion — a returned summary, a graph reaching its end, a workflow returning — so the interval between that moment and acceptance exists in none of them and exists in every business obligation [R3 §10.1, R3 §9]. Shipped issue trackers permit a work item to be Done with no resolution, so finished and open are simultaneously true in one product [R5-13]. And for a job nobody anticipated there is no fixed pool and no regression case, so the acceptance owner must be a human or a deterministic predicate rather than a model checker at its highest-variance point [R7 §8 F-1].
axes.discriminating_question: Who is accountable for a piece of work between producer-declared completion and acceptance, what is that state called, and can it be queried?

axes.topic: The founder as an instrument with an unmeasured error rate
axes.account: Human evaluators agree with each other 5–65% of the time, agree on severity 20–28%, and in two studies not a single problem was unanimously judged severe [R7 F15]. Nothing in the package states an expected human error rate or requires it to be measured, while every design eventually routes to human acceptance [R7 §9]. The founder's distinct value is that his errors are uncorrelated with the model family's, which is also why his absence is expensive in a specific way the queue rule must name [R7 §8 F-6].
axes.discriminating_question: What is the expected error rate of the human acceptance step, who measures it, and with what uncertainty is it reported beside the model instruments it is meant to anchor?

axes.topic: The metered-path affordance as an account property
axes.account: A founder constraint forbids silent fallback to a metered path. Both providers surface a purchase-credits path at the exact moment of exhaustion, and one prompts to raise or remove a spend limit without leaving the tool; enabling credits also shortens the prompt-cache lifetime [R8 W-5]. Whether the path is disabled is an observable account setting, not a property of any architecture, and nothing in the package observes it [R8 TC-26(b)].
axes.discriminating_question: Who observes the account setting, how often, and what record is made when it changes?

falsifiers.headline: DIRECT OBSERVATION. Zero of the fourteen candidates examined is a falsifier against one of the six fixed boundaries. Two are falsifiers against a strength the frozen protocol §6 grants to the simple baseline B0. Five are conformance counterexamples against the runtime or against a founder constraint — they refute the assumption that a boundary holds without being built, not the boundary. One is a criterion tension argued as a preference, and its own lane declines to advance it as a counterexample. Every lane that touched a fixed boundary stated in its own words that it was reopening none.

entries.target: protocol §6 comparator strength — B0 has 'the lowest plausible consumption of scarce subscription capacity'
entries.verdict: FALSIFIER of a protocol §6 granted strength, not of a fixed boundary
entries.note: Four provider mechanisms documented in primary vendor material: the full conversation is resent with every request, a break longer than the cache lifetime reprocesses the whole context, compaction is itself a large request, and idle check-ins send full context. B0 minimises launches and not the weekly bucket. R8 did not amend the frozen protocol and said so; it recorded that a round which measures B0 without these four will measure launches and report them as allowance.

entries.target: protocol §6 comparator definition — B0 is 'one long-context session'
entries.verdict: FALSIFIER of a protocol §6 comparator premise, not of a fixed boundary
entries.note: Derived from the package's own launch contract rather than an external source: a native job defaults to a 360-second network window, so a six-hour single context cannot run and continuation is mandatory in EVERY arm. B0 keeps all its other legitimate strengths and loses this one. The consequence is that the handoff cost is not avoidable by refusing to split work; it is avoidable only by typing what crosses the boundary.

entries.target: the authority invariant — no component silently inherits all permissions of the process that created it
entries.verdict: CONFORMANCE COUNTEREXAMPLE against the runtime, not a falsifier of the boundary
entries.note: Four documented default inheritance paths. R4's own disposition is that the constraint is coherent and implementable and must be BUILT rather than assumed. The invariant is not weakened; the assumption that it holds for free is.

findings: R1 §8 'Against the fixed boundary of consequence and release'
entries.verdict: CONSTRAINT ON IMPLEMENTATION, explicitly not a reopening
entries.note: R1 states it in its own words: any design placing a release boundary inside a component with a measured 16–51% failure rate has put it in the wrong place. The boundary must be the loader and the outbound channel. 'This does not reopen the boundary; it constrains where it may be implemented.' R4 F12 reaches the same conclusion from the sandbox side.

entries.verdict: EVIDENCE GAP IN THE FIELD, not a falsifier — and it strengthens the boundary's status as a design obligation
entries.note: No surveyed system has an acceptance-owner concept; every one terminates on producer-declared completion. R3 states this is a gap in the field rather than in its survey, and that the acceptance boundary is the one part of the specification that cannot be imported from any of these systems.

Every surveyed system is a software-construction or generic-orchestration system and no evidence bears on customs disputes, refunds, supplier commitments or wind-down. The W11 narrowing risk is therefore a risk of importing the evidence base, not only the vocabulary.

entries.target: negative control §4.2 — a shared source of truth nobody is forced to read
entries.verdict: CONFIRMATION of a negative control, with a primary source
entries.note: Three vendors have built exactly the artifact the control says must fail, and two document in their own words that it is not enforcement and that contradictions may be resolved arbitrarily. A candidate proposing shared state as instruction text has proposed a thing already built three times and documented as non-binding. R3 F4 and R3 F16 reach the same conclusion from two of the same vendors and one other.

entries.target: evidence and acceptance under one model family
entries.verdict: NAMES A RESIDUAL the boundary must disclose; explicitly not a reopening
entries.note: Independence of INFLUENCE is achievable by procedure and measurable. Independence of ERROR is decided in the negative for self-consistent errors and no procedure converts one into the other. R7 states it reopens no fixed boundary and routes no decision packet. The specification is already correct on this point; what is missing is the measurement, not the decision.

entries.verdict: SPECIFIC DEFECT IN A FROZEN FIXTURE, classed (b) by R7 itself
entries.note: F-4's adverse variation plants a known defect and supplies the producer's rationale but does not require the PAIRED CLEAN CASE that negative control §4.3 and the specification both require. Given measured false-positive rates of 68.4–96.8% on already-patched files, an unpaired known-defect control cannot distinguish a working checker from one that refuses everything. R7 also proposes a third arm (rationale versus preferred conclusion are distinct leakage channels) and a stated floor for 'a measurable difference between arms'.

entries.target: the founder constraint forbidding silent metered fallback
entries.verdict: CONFORMANCE GAP with a named observation point, not a falsifier
entries.note: The policy is stated and nothing enforces it; the path is a documented in-product affordance at both providers, surfaced at the moment of exhaustion. Whether it is disabled is an account setting nobody observes.

entries.target: dimension W11, which fails a candidate described as 'a roster of digital employees'
entries.verdict: PREFERENCE with an argument — R8 itself declines to advance it as a counterexample
entries.note: W11 and W12 pull in opposite directions: the structure easiest for a founder to hold is the one W11 rejects by name. R8 records it as 'a criterion tension, not a defect', and says W11 encodes a conclusion the round has not reached. It is the closest thing in the round to an argument against a frozen criterion, and it is not a counterexample.

entries.target: a support the package cites, not a boundary
entries.note: The standard most often cited for handling unanticipated work admits a pre-declared item that was not pre-scheduled; it does not admit an unanticipated KIND of work. The package's retention of adaptive cases is therefore weaker support for TC-19 than it reads.

entries.target: how a claim may be scored, not a boundary
entries.verdict: INVERSE OF A FALSIFIER — a warning that a definitional truth is positioned where an empirical result would go
entries.note: The safety clause of TC-21 is entailed by the already-frozen boundaries at any demand level, so no experiment is needed or possible for it. R8 asks the round to split the claim and not let a definitional truth stand as evidence for the empirical one.

entries.verdict: MEASUREMENT-INTEGRITY FINDING against the repository, not a boundary falsifier
entries.note: Two numeric ranges carried in an internal decision record and repeated in two sections of an internal design document cannot be traced from the repository's own citation, while a third section of the same document states the traceable version with 'verified' beside it. R7 does not assert the figures are wrong, only that they are untraceable and therefore folklore under the evidence rules. The unverifiable version is what propagated into the brief R7 was given.

measurement_gaps.gap: No lane executed any experiment; there is no runtime. Every measurement cited in the round is about some other system, on some other task distribution, at some other date.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: R7 names the one instrument buildable cheaply and repeatedly deferred: a seeded-defect corpus. Until it exists, every statement about this system's verification quality is a transfer from published work on other systems.

measurement_gaps.gap: The concurrency pin blocks the stated measures of TC-03, TC-20 and TC-39 wholly, and TC-22's parallelism half. Raising it is circular: the measurement that sets the threshold requires first changing the parameter being measured.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: Establish whether the pin is a provider constraint or a self-imposed policy by inspecting the account entitlement. If policy, a staged revision as an experiment with its own stopping rule; if a constraint, record the threshold as permanently unknown in this system and say so in those words.

measurement_gaps.gap: There is no absolute denominator for scarce capacity on the provider side, so no arm can be expressed as a fraction of the week.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: None available. The honest disposition is that every capacity finding in this round is a RATIO between arms, stated as such, and that any downstream decision requiring a fraction cannot be taken on this evidence.

measurement_gaps.gap: The joint false-acceptance rate of a same-family producer/verifier pair on a controlled planted-defect set has never been published, and it is the quantity TC-11's own measure and the specification both demand.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: Plant defects on a fixed corpus; run producer self-check and separate-context checker; count joint false acceptance, with a paired clean case in the same session and the result reported as a false-positive rate rather than a verdict.

measurement_gaps.gap: No source measures facts lost per handoff in an agentic system carrying real obligations, and no probe stratifies facts from constraints.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: The claim's own recall probe, run STRATIFIED — operational facts separately from exclusions, deadlines, promised remedies and rejected alternatives — with the continuation boundary instrumented in both arms.

measurement_gaps.gap: The arrival rate of genuinely novel kinds of work is not established by any source; the one figure located was vendor marketing and was excluded. The rate decides whether any recogniser can work at all.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: The cheapest measurement in the entire round and it needs no runtime: count admitted items over a past window of the founder's own history against the existing capability list.

measurement_gaps.gap: What one compaction event loses, in load-bearing facts rather than tokens, is unmeasured by anyone including the vendor.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: Available today at the cost of one field read per response: reconcile the provider's reported applied-edits against the manifest and treat any unaccounted edit as a manifest defect.

measurement_gaps.gap: No published selection-degradation curve exists for a Claude-family model over a real skill library; every curve located came from other model families or retrieval encoders.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: The 10/100/1000 sweep with adversarial near-duplicates, with the near-duplicates authored by a process other than the one that authored the library, per negative control §4.10.

measurement_gaps.gap: Whether a shared authoritative view increases or decreases duplicated external effects is unmeasured; the only measurement of correlated duplication was taken with no shared state at all.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: R1 calls it the single most valuable experiment named in its report: two executors, one shared next-action view, an idempotency-key collision counter and a rate anomaly monitor on the shared resource.

measurement_gaps.gap: No study decomposes a role into its label and its procedural content and measures each.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: R2 calls it the cleanest experiment nobody has run: three arms — label plus procedure, procedure only, label only — on one fixture at matched executor count.

measurement_gaps.gap: Whether the set of instantiated executor profiles converges over time is measured by nothing, and it is the only honest test of whether capability differentiation is a roster by another name.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: Run for a month and count distinct profiles.

measurement_gaps.gap: Whether this repository's declared tool scoping binds at runtime is recorded as unverified by the repository itself while the vendor documents it as a client-applied filter.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: One call. Dispatch the read-only reviewer, whose tool list omits the shell, and attempt a single shell command.

measurement_gaps.gap: Why an identical grant delivered 24 tools on one date and zero on three dispatches two days later, configuration unchanged, is unknown; R3 calls it the most operationally consequential unknown in its set.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: Observe the grant at the effect rather than in the configuration — the verifying command currently checks configuration only.

measurement_gaps.gap: False exclusion — correct work refused because a filter was too tight — is measured by nobody. Every privacy and filtering source measures leakage only.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: Run the paired clean case in the same session as every adverse case, and report both numbers or neither.

measurement_gaps.gap: Not one source reports authoring or maintenance effort in any unit, so the maintenance half of the specialist-versus-skill comparison cannot be evaluated.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: The 'domain that changes' fixture: change one rule the domain depends on and count what must be edited, retested and revalidated under each unit.

measurement_gaps.gap: No source tests an omitted DUTY in an otherwise valid skill; the closest studies omitted implementation elements on software tasks.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: The conformance case already specified: a skill that passes every shape check whose worked example omits a cancellation duty.

measurement_gaps.gap: Whether the high-risk-system record-keeping obligation is in scope for any of the four ventures is undetermined and unowned.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: A scope determination, not an experiment. If in scope, the manifest stops being a design choice and its cost argument closes.

measurement_gaps.gap: Whether the metered path is disabled on the actual accounts is unobserved.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: Read the account setting. It is observable today and costs nothing.

measurement_gaps.gap: Whether the founder-competence transfer test, or any human error rate, has ever been measured — in this package or in the literature.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: The delayed unfamiliar-transfer test as already specified: after an absence, measure recognition and intervention performance on material the founder did not see being produced. Attendance, confidence and agreement are explicitly not competence.

measurement_gaps.gap: No published measurement of coordination cost at a concurrency of two exists; every figure located assumes concurrency this system does not admit.
measurement_gaps.cheapest_experiment: Measure coordination minutes and transmitted context bytes separately from work performed, at the concurrency actually available.

cross_lane_questions.method: Every item each lane listed under 'questions other lanes may have missed', checked against the other seven reports. 'answered' means another lane's finding resolves it; 'partial' means another lane supplies the mechanism, the measurement or half the answer; 'open' means no lane in this round addresses it.

items.question: Who measures false exclusion — correct work refused because the loader filtered too hard?
items.note: Both supply the paired-clean-case mechanism; neither measures the rate. Becomes axis X17.

items.question: Does shared truth increase duplicated external effects?
items.note: R5-22 and R3 §8 record duplication under vague delegation, not under shared truth. R1 names this its most valuable unrun experiment.

items.question: What is the writer authority on shared state, and what happens on a conflicting write?
items.note: Single-writer concurrency keyed per entity is the only surveyed mechanism answering it structurally; state-write-as-event makes state and audit one artifact.

items.question: Is the manifest's 'actual delivered inputs' rule satisfiable across the provider boundary at all?
items.note: Partially, by counts; three transforms in one substrate and none records what it dropped.

items.question: What is the unit of a peer work projection, and who decides its recipient scope?
items.note: R7 §9 sharpens it into a leakage question and does not answer it.

items.question: Does any fixture actually put conflicting context in one window?
items.note: Independently the same answer: 'isolated context' must be split into isolation-for-attention and isolation-for-confidentiality, and only the second is exercised by any fixture in the frozen set.

items.question: What is the retention and deletion story for a peer projection?
items.note: R6 §9 Q5 is the same shape for skills and is also open.

items.question: Is the high-risk-system record-keeping obligation in scope for any of the four ventures?
items.note: Unowned by any lane.

items.question: What is the smallest work order that can complete inside one launch window, and does the answer change what 'one unit of work' means?
Does a continuation count as a handoff?
items.note: The mechanism is documented — a continuation is one of three lossy transforms none of which records what it dropped — but no lane decides whether it is held to the typed-constraint discipline. Becomes axis X12.

items.question: Which of the 46 capabilities carry constraints that would not survive a 25-word compression?
items.note: Now a computable audit rather than a worry.

items.question: Is any executor in a candidate justified by a reason not on the founder's list, and does it say so?
items.note: No candidate exists yet.

items.question: What false-positive rate is this system willing to accept from a verifier?
items.note: R7 measures the shape and asks the same question about capacity. Two lanes independently identify the number as unowned.

items.question: If concurrency stays at two non-interchangeable slots, does 'parallel work' belong on the list at all right now?
items.note: Corroborated as unmeasurable; the disposition — real in general and inert in this deployment — remains a founder decision.

items.question: Who re-checks an expired transfer, so a 2023 measurement does not justify a 2026 structure?
items.note: Model pinning in the evaluation harness and the removal-test question supply the mechanism; no owner is named.

items.question: Does the claim that a loaded prose package cannot spend survive contact with the actual launcher?
items.note: Independently, no. Two lanes read the same vendor page and returned the same answer.

items.question: Who is accountable between producer-declared completion and acceptance?
items.note: R5-13 shows the shipped precedent permits the contradiction. Becomes axis X18.

items.question: What is the answer when an instruction file and an enforcement rule disagree?
items.note: For this runtime the precedence is documented and deny is unconditional; what remains undocumented is what a system should DO when the two encode different intents.

items.question: Is delegation depth a policy, a resource limit or a safety property?
items.note: R4 sharpens it: spawning costs no permission check, so the ceiling needs an owner and a checkpoint. Disagreement D-10.

items.question: Can a grant be observed to have arrived, as distinct from having been declared?
items.note: R3 F59 is the only evidence that it sometimes does not; R4 supplies the mechanism that would observe it at the effect. Becomes axis X16.

items.question: Does approving a tool at install time approve the text the model will read at call time?
items.note: No. Three lanes converge: the registry binds a name to an owner, annotations are normatively untrusted, and skill metadata from outside the trust boundary must not be trusted.

items.question: Which harness mechanisms carry a removal test?
items.note: R3 F39 is the field's clearest instance of one that did.

items.question: What is the unit of capacity when the provider bills a subscription?
items.note: The separated units exist in the package; no absolute denominator exists, so every finding is a ratio. R3 adds a constraint R8 does not carry: one vendor prohibits building a product on subscription authentication.

items.question: If the summary of a run is the only thing that survives it, what carries the omissions?
items.note: The mechanism is named — reconcile the provider's applied-edits against the manifest — and is implemented nowhere.

items.question: Does anything in the surveyed field measure whether its human operator is still competent?
items.note: No, in three independent source sets.

items.question: Is 'role' one concept or two?
items.note: Two. Both lanes also flag that the decomposition that would settle which half carries the benefit is unrun.

items.question: Does this system have a credential at the boundary at all?
items.note: R4 believes it load-bearing and unresolvable from documentation. Every attenuation mechanism assumes a token exists that can be narrowed; a subscription session's authority is settings files and hook decisions. If nothing can be attenuated, the constraint must be enforced by mediation, which is a different architecture.

items.question: Who owns an agent definition file, and is writing one a consequence-class action?
items.note: R6 supplies a second path through a knowledge artifact and R3 shows declarations that bind nothing; no lane assigns the ownership.

items.question: Is delegation itself an authority operation?
items.note: Spawning costs no permission check in this runtime; fan-out, depth and cost all follow from a call nothing gates.

items.question: Can a low-consequence action compose into a high-consequence one?
items.note: Read plus read plus send is three low-consequence actions and one disclosure; nothing in a per-action class detects the composition.

items.question: Does approval expire?
items.note: The runtime's permanent allow rules show what happens when it does not. R5-12's terminating escalation ladder is the routing analogue.

items.question: What is the unit of identity for a work attempt?
items.note: The runtime exposes both an instance identifier and a type; if the acceptance record names a role and the enforcement record names an instance, the two cannot be joined after an incident.

items.question: Who may raise a ceiling, and how is that act distinguished from using one?
items.note: One cloud provider separates them structurally: a permissions boundary does not grant.

items.question: Is the escalation classifier in scope for the injection it is judging?
items.note: R7 F8 and F11 make it sharper — framing moves the threshold — and nobody answers it.

items.question: Is the thesis a blackboard architecture?
items.note: R5's own finding. R1 and R8 work near it and neither names the source. If it is, two claims are one question with a forty-year-old primary that declines to answer it and prices each answer.

items.question: What is the base rate of novel work?
items.note: The cheapest measurement in the round and the one that decides whether any recogniser can work.

items.question: Does the refusal path have its own acceptance owner?
items.note: A communicated refusal is an outward effect. R3 §10.1's interval question is the general form.

items.question: Is re-routing scored as a defect anywhere in the package?
items.note: If so, the system will be tuned to suppress the mechanism by which the right owner is found. Disagreement D-12.

items.question: Who owns the triage queue's own backlog?
items.note: A rotation with no service level is an unowned queue with a name.

items.question: What is the alarm on the unroutable destination, and who is paged by it?
items.note: A named destination with no reader is the original failure with better records.

items.question: When no mandate covers the harm at all, does the least-authority default have a terminal element, and is that element a person?
items.note: R7 argues from near-chance model judgement on novel objectively-checkable material that novel-work acceptance must be human or deterministic; it does not name the terminal element.

items.question: Is the authority to add work to a live case separately granted from the authority to perform it?
items.note: One standard separates them explicitly; the package does not appear to. R4 §9 Q7 is the same distinction in the authority lane and is also open.

items.question: Does any mechanism in the package count overflows?
items.note: Shedding without a count is indistinguishable from a silent drop after the fact.

items.question: What does 'done' mean when the resolution field is empty?
items.note: The shipped precedent permits the contradiction and the protocol's (d)-class example 3 says it blocks.

items.question: Who owns a skill's expiry date?
items.note: No shipping format has a field for a review date or an invalidation trigger; the knowledge custodian owns claims, not procedures. R1's temporal-validity constituent is the general form.

items.question: What reaches the selection surface — what is the lossy projection from a full skill package to its selectable description?
items.note: R6 calls it a context manifest for the selection step that nobody has claimed. R1 owns manifests and does not cover it.

items.question: Is skill selection itself a significant run requiring a manifest?
Does a skill count as an external effect when it grants a tool, and which component refuses that?
items.note: R4 answers the enforcement half — refusal must be observed at the effect via a hook keyed on the caller's identity — and leaves the component assignment open.

items.question: How does a skill get retired when it is cited by a live claim or pinned by an accepted run?
What is the unit of the selection budget under a subscription?
items.note: Answered negatively: there is no denominator, so the conversion R6 asks for cannot be computed today.

items.question: Who authors the adversarial near-duplicates for the library sweep?
items.note: Near-duplicates authored by the same process that authored the library will not be adversarial in the way the measurement requires, and negative control §4.10 constrains the timing.

items.question: Does the shared source of truth become the preference-leakage channel that defeats provenance separation?
items.note: The sharpest adverse question against the thesis's central mechanism. A producer writes its framing into the canonical record, a checker reads the record, and every provenance check passes. R1 owns state and does not cover it.

items.question: Does a half-satisfiable criterion justify a separate agent, or a separate context and input set?
items.note: Two lanes arrive at the same place from opposite directions. Becomes axis X11.

items.question: Who checks the checker's inputs?
items.note: R1 F-21 shows no standard in the path carries the fields that would attest it, so the independence claim rests on a record the system generated about itself.

items.question: At what detection rate does a checker stop being worth its capacity?
items.note: Blocked upstream by the missing denominator.

items.question: What is the human anchor's own error rate?
items.note: Measured in the literature for human evaluators generally; unstated and unrequired in the package. Becomes axis X19.

items.question: Is 'no runtime exists' protecting a wrong number?
items.note: Every measurement the lane cites is about someone else's system; the one instrument buildable cheaply has been repeatedly deferred.

items.question: Is the set of instantiated executor profiles stable over a month?
items.note: The only honest test of whether capability differentiation is a roster discovered rather than declared.

items.question: Who owns a reservation, when reservations are held by class and a class has no representative?
items.note: R5's ownership resolver assigns custody by rule and does not answer which component yields when two protected classes need the same slot.

items.question: What is the denominator for scarce capacity?
items.note: Answered negatively by its own lane and uncontradicted; R6 §9 Q6 asks the same and is blocked by it.

items.question: What does idle reserved capacity cost?
items.note: Allowance does not roll over across its reset window, so a conservative scheduler destroys what it withholds — the opposite of how a reserve behaves under per-token pricing.

items.question: Is the metered path disabled on the actual accounts today?
items.note: An account setting nobody observes. Becomes axis X20.

items.question: If a provider doubled or halved the allowance overnight, would any decision in this round change?
items.note: If none would, the capacity argument was never load-bearing and should stop being cited as one.

items.question: Is the concurrency pin a provider constraint or a policy?
items.note: The highest-leverage open question in the round: it gates the disposition of four claim verdicts. Becomes axis X14.

items.question: When does the simple baseline stop being the simple baseline?

census.method: Statement kinds are counted from the DIRECTIVE §6 label each lane attached to each numbered finding, taking the FIRST label where a finding carries two (several are 'source claim + inference'), so inference is undercounted by design and the separately-headed inference blocks are reported alongside. Source rows are counted from each lane's own source table, and 'declared interest' is counted from that table's own conflict-of-interest column, including academic author-interest where the lane wrote one. Anthropic-family rows are counted separately because every lane shares that family and therefore cannot treat those rows as external.

Also discloses that its fetch layer summarised pages before the lane saw them, so no quotation was verified character for character.

headline_for_step_3: INFERENCE. About seven in ten source rows across the round carry a declared vendor, author or commercial interest, and roughly one in five of all rows is the lanes' own model family reporting on its own products. A Step 3 framer that treats the evidence base as neutral is treating a vendor corpus as neutral.

DIRECT OBSERVATION. The two lanes whose subject IS vendor documentation — frameworks and skills — are the two most vendor-dependent, at 35 of 37 and 27 of 28 rows with a declared interest. Their two least-conflicted rows are the matched-budget papers, and those rows carry the round's most cross-cutting result.

DIRECT OBSERVATION. The verification and routing lanes are the least dependent on the lanes' own vendor: 2 Anthropic rows each. The economics lane is the most exposed in the place it matters least — 9 of 24 rows are the provider describing its own allowance, and the quantity that binds is the one the provider stopped publishing.

DIRECT OBSERVATION. Source claims outnumber facts and direct observations by a wide margin in every lane. The four direct-observation-heavy blocks are the frameworks lane's reading of this repository, the skills lane's reading of its own library, the authority lane's single tool-absence report, and the verification lane's correction against this repository's own records. The round's own artifacts are therefore the only things anybody in it OBSERVED rather than read about.

DIRECT OBSERVATION. No claim was registered by any lane. Seven of eight report the claim-registration tool absent from their session while the roster declares the grant; the eighth declined on its own judgement, reasoning that registering an inference would launder it. The consequence is that NOT ONE QUOTE in this round has been machine-verified against its URL by the source resolver, and the round therefore carries the same declared-versus-delivered gap it identifies as a finding (axis X16).

five_criteria.disposition: supported, and the strongest of the five
five_criteria.why: It is the only one enforced outside the model and the only one with a published price: a capability-based separation solved 77% of benchmark tasks with provable security against 84% undefended [R2 F-09]. But in the runtime you would use, a helper inherits every tool by default, an escalated mode propagates downward, and a skill file can grant tools for the turn that loads it [R4 F5, R2 F-08, R6 F7]. It is a reason that works and it has to be built.

five_criteria.disposition: real, and the word covers two different things
five_criteria.why: Isolation for attention moves with the model generation and is shrinking. Isolation for confidentiality is structural and does not. Separated topologies cut disclosure violations by 20 to 50 points and still leave over 75% [R1 F-15], and separation at the process and credential level does not happen at all by default [R4 F5]. Only the confidentiality sense is exercised by any of your six fixtures [R2 §8].

five_criteria.disposition: real as a requirement, half achievable
five_criteria.why: You can stop the producer influencing the checker, and that is measurable. You cannot make their errors independent inside one model family, and no blinding reaches it [R7 TC-37, R7 F13]. The best procedurally independent reviewer anyone has measured found under a third of planted defects [R7 F9].

five_criteria.disposition: real in general, close to inert in this deployment
five_criteria.why: Whether splitting pays is a property of the PARTITION, not of the job: cohesion-aware splitting gained 11 to 14 points, poor splitting degraded both speed and quality [R2 F-06]. And your concurrency policy admits two slots that are not interchangeable, so the criterion can be exercised at most once per work order [R2 F-19].

No source separates it from a versioned skill [R6 TC-33], and role labels alone showed no measured benefit across 162 roles and 2,410 questions [R6 F6, R2 F-10]. What separates an agent from a skill, on the evidence, is a context window, a permission set and a model — not knowledge.

At least five candidate sixth reasons survived adversarial search across three lanes: input provenance, provider or account separation, consequence class, attributable identity, and — for people only — a differently-correlated error source [R2 F-21, R4 F4, R7 §8 F-6]. Whether to close the list is your decision, not a research finding.

four_costs.disposition: real, measured, and aimed at the wrong target
four_costs.why: Operational facts survive a compressed transfer at about 0.97; the rules, exclusions and promises survive at about 0.57. Vague constraint language leaked in 73% of cases; a typed constraint list leaked in 0 of 48 [R2 F-04].

four_costs.disposition: real in direction, folklore in magnitude, and the wrong unit
four_costs.why: The most-quoted multiple is a vendor self-report with no published method; five lanes found it independently and all five flagged it [AG-14]. Under a subscription the unit is allowance, and the provider stopped publishing the number [R8 W-6].
It cannot be stated without the realised concurrency count beside it, and at your current policy that count is at most two [R2 TC-03].
It is a cost of any context transformation, including inside one session, and it is mandatory here because a job caps at a 360-second window — so the single-agent arm owes it too [R2 F-13, R2 F-18].

what_is_now_known.nobody_could_measure: There is no runtime and no lane ran an experiment. Four of your cost claims cannot be measured at the current concurrency at all, and raising it is circular [MG-02]. There is no denominator for scarce capacity, so every capacity figure here is a ratio between two arms and never a fraction of your week [MG-03]. Nobody has measured the joint false-acceptance rate of a producer and a same-family checker [MG-04], what one compaction event loses in facts rather than tokens [MG-07], whether a shared view raises or lowers duplicated effects [MG-09], or how often genuinely new kinds of work arrive [MG-06]. The last of those is the cheapest thing on the list and needs no software: count admitted work over a past window against what you already knew how to do.
three_most_decision_relevant: How you cut matters more than whether you cut. Automatically generated multi-agent systems underperformed a single agent at up to ten times the cost, while an expert-designed one reached 96.5% against 57.0% on the same diagnostic — in the same paper. Two lanes found it separately and both say the same thing: the discriminator is whether the separation is enforced by construction or merely described in prompts [R2 F-03, R3 F52].

The defence against a false entry in shared state does not work against the kind of false entry that matters. A poisoning attack carrying no instruction and no role manipulation passed a four-stage screen 360 times out of 360, while the same screen caught injections at 0.832 recall. The ranking defence was indistinguishable from no defence at its shipped setting, and at the setting that worked it took evidence recall to zero [R1 F-10].

Under a subscription, the architecture does not change what you spend. It changes the date on which work stops, and unused allowance is destroyed rather than saved [R8 §3]. That inverts the usual question from 'which design costs more' to 'which design reaches the wall sooner, and who decides what is shed when it does'.
what_is_now_known.one_thing_about_the_round_itself: No lane could register a single claim. Seven of the eight report the registration tool absent from their session while the roster says the grant exists; the eighth declined on its own judgement. So no quotation in this round has been machine-checked against its source, and the round reproduced, in its own operation, the declared-versus-delivered gap it identifies as a finding.
